# SPI Read Command Processor Specification

## 1. Overview

The SPI read command processor handles the execution of SPI flash read commands. It is responsible for:

- Capturing the read command address from the SPI bit stream.
- Requesting data from the correct internal data region: read buffer, mailbox, or SFDP.
- Sequencinag any mode-byte or dummy-cycle phases required by the command.
- Presenting read data to the SPI output serializer in the I/O mode selected by the command.
- Reporting read progress for software-managed double-buffering and watermark tracking.

The module is a read-only datapath. It does not process write or program commands.

The supported command classes are:

- Normal Read.
- Fast Read.
- Fast Read Dual Output.
- Fast Read Quad Output.
- Read SFDP.
- Read commands that access the mailbox address region when the mailbox feature is enabled.

Commands that include a mode byte are handled by consuming and ignoring the mode byte. Continuous-read mode is not implemented.

---

## 2. Activation and Idle Behavior

The module must remain idle unless it is selected to process a read command or an SFDP read.

While idle:

- No address bytes shall be captured.
- No output data shall be presented.
- No data memory requests shall be issued.
- No mailbox line-control indication shall be asserted.
- No watermark or buffer-flip events shall be generated.

The module shall be able to begin a new command after reset or after the previous SPI transaction has ended.

Some state is intentionally kept across SPI transactions:

- The active read-buffer half indicator.
- The last read address reported for software.

These are cleared only by the system reset, not by the end of an SPI transaction.

---

## 3. Command Information Requirements

Before the module begins the address phase, the command information for the received opcode must be valid and must describe:

- A valid address mode: 3-byte, 4-byte, or configuration-dependent.
- A payload direction of output.
- The output I/O width: single, dual, or quad.
- Whether a dummy phase is required.
- Whether a mode-byte phase is required.
- The dummy-cycle count.

If the address mode is configuration-dependent, the module shall use the global 4-byte address enable to decide whether the command uses a 3-byte or 4-byte address.

If the command information does not describe a valid output read command, the module is not required to produce read data.

---

## 4. Address Phase

After activation, the module shall enter the address phase and assemble the read address from the incoming serial data.

### 4.1 Address Width

- For a 3-byte address mode, the effective address is 24 bits. The upper byte of the address shall be treated as zero for data-memory access.
- For a 4-byte address mode, the full 32-bit address shall be captured.
- For SFDP reads, the address is treated as a 24-bit address. The upper 16 bits are ignored; only the lower 8 bits select the offset within the SFDP data region.

### 4.2 Address Capture

The module shall accept address bytes as they are completed by the serial-to-parallel converter.

For the currently supported read command types, the address is received on the single SPI input line. The module shall assemble the address in the order the bytes are received.

The module shall make the first data-memory read request as soon as the word-aligned address is known, without waiting for the final address byte to complete. This is required so that read data is available when the output phase begins.

At the end of the address phase, the module shall choose the next phase as follows:

- If a mode-byte phase is enabled, proceed to the mode-byte phase.
- Otherwise, if a dummy phase is enabled, proceed to the dummy phase.
- Otherwise, proceed directly to the output phase.

---

## 5. Mode-Byte Phase

If the command information enables a mode-byte phase:

- The module shall wait for one mode byte from the SPI host.
- The value of the mode byte shall be ignored.
- After the mode byte is received, the module shall proceed to the dummy phase.

The module does not implement continuous-read mode and shall not change address or data behavior based on the mode-byte value.

---

## 6. Dummy Phase

If the command information enables a dummy phase:

- The module shall wait for the configured number of dummy SPI clock cycles.
- During this phase, no valid read data shall be presented to the output serializer.
- After the dummy cycle count is exhausted, the module shall enter the output phase.

The dummy-cycle count is taken from the command information entry.

---

## 7. Output Phase

The output phase begins after the address phase, and after any mode-byte or dummy phase.

### 7.1 Data Presentation

At the start of the output phase, the module shall:

- Indicate that output has started.
- Present the first read data byte to the output serializer.
- Set the I/O mode according to the command payload width:
  - Single output for single-lane read commands.
  - Dual output for dual-lane read commands.
  - Quad output for quad-lane read commands.

The output data shall be timed to the output-side SPI clock.

### 7.2 Continuous Byte Stream

The module shall continue to present sequential data bytes for as long as the SPI transaction remains active.

After each data byte is completed on the SPI lines:

- The current byte address shall be incremented by one.
- The next buffered byte shall be made available for output.
- The read address tracking output shall be updated.

The output phase shall begin without an extra wait cycle. The module assumes that the read data pipeline has the first byte ready when output starts and that subsequent bytes are prefetched in time.

### 7.3 Address Increment

Address increments are performed only for bytes actually sent during the output phase. Prefetch activity must not by itself advance the reported read address or trigger watermark or flip events.

---

## 8. Data Region Selection

The module shall request read data from one of three internal memory regions, depending on the command:

- Read buffer.
- Mailbox buffer.
- SFDP buffer.

### 8.1 Read Buffer Access

For ordinary read commands, data shall be read from the read buffer. The address used for the read-buffer access is derived from the received command address and is limited to the read-buffer address space.

### 8.2 Mailbox Access

When the mailbox feature is enabled, the module shall compare the received address against the configured mailbox base address. The comparison shall ignore the low offset bits that correspond to the mailbox buffer size.

If the address falls inside the mailbox region:

- All read requests for that command shall be directed to the mailbox buffer instead of the read buffer.
- The read address reported for software shall not be updated for this command.
- Watermark and buffer-flip events shall not be generated for this command.

The mailbox base address must be aligned to the mailbox buffer size. If it is not aligned, mailbox hit behavior is not defined.

### 8.3 Mailbox Line-Control Indication

When the mailbox feature is enabled, the address hits the mailbox region, and mailbox interception is also enabled, the module shall assert the mailbox line-control indicator.

This indicator is used by the enclosing SPI device to prevent the downstream flash device from driving the SPI lines while the module is servicing a mailbox read internally.

### 8.4 SFDP Access

When the module is selected for an SFDP read:

- Data shall always be read from the SFDP data region.
- The SFDP region selection shall take priority over mailbox or read-buffer selection.
- The received address lower 8 bits select the offset within the SFDP region.
- The upper address bits are ignored and do not affect the SFDP data location.

---

## 9. Read Address Reporting

The module shall provide a read-address output for software.

This output shall contain the current byte address of an ordinary read-buffer read command.

The read address output shall be updated:

- As address bytes are received during the address phase.
- After each data byte is transmitted during the output phase.

The output shall not be updated for:

- SFDP reads.
- Mailbox reads when the mailbox feature is enabled.

The read address output shall persist between SPI transactions and shall be cleared only by system reset.

---

## 10. Double-Buffering and Watermark Events

The read buffer is organized as two 1 kB buffers. The module shall support software management of these buffers by generating event pulses at the appropriate points during read-buffer accesses.

### 10.1 Watermark Event

A watermark event shall be generated when, during an ordinary read-buffer read, the byte address first crosses the software-configured watermark threshold within the current 1 kB buffer.

The event must be based on bytes actually transmitted on the SPI interface. Prefetching data from memory must not trigger the watermark event.

The watermark event shall be generated only once per buffer until the active buffer half is changed.

### 10.2 Buffer-Flip Event

A buffer-flip event shall be generated when a read sequence crosses from the current 1 kB read buffer half into the other half.

When this event occurs, the module shall also toggle the internally selected active buffer half for subsequent read requests.

The active-buffer state and the flip behavior shall persist across SPI transactions so that software can refill the inactive buffer while the host continues reading from the active buffer.

### 10.3 Suppressed Events

Watermark and flip events shall be suppressed for:

- SFDP reads.
- Mailbox reads when the mailbox feature is enabled.

---

## 11. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module must:

- Return to the idle state.
- Deassert output valid.
- Clear the reported read address.
- Clear the mailbox line-control indicator.
- Clear any pending event pulses.
- Select the initial read-buffer half.

After reset, the module shall be ready to process a new read command when selected by the command parser.
